scripts.universe_source: SignalMasterTable (base panel L91-92; monthlyCRSP shrout left-joined L96-101; m_aCompustat left-joined L104-122; IBES left-joined on tickerIBES L138-142)
scripts.fill_semantics: No panel-wide fills. Two value-level fallbacks, both only on rows surviving the June+screen sample: (1) ceq_ave (L163-172): if first row per permno (row_num==0) OR l12_ceq null -> ceq_ave=ceq, else (ceq+l12_ceq)/2 — a per-permno-position conditional fill; (2) FROE3 (L229-239): when LTG null -> FROE3=FROE2, else feps2*(1+LTG/100)*shrout/((ceq1+ceq2)/2). All three saved factors pass through save_predictor which drops null rows. Annual values are then tiled to 12 monthly copies (offsets 0-11mo from the June time_avail_m, L449-462) regardless of whether the permno still exists in CRSP in those months.
scripts.nan_aggregation: AnalystValue = sum of 4 terms / mve (L279-312): any null term (e.g., null FROE2 impossible post-screen since feps2 required, but null k or null shrout) nulls the whole value. IntrinsicValue needs ROE (screens ALLOW ROE null, L255) -> null ROE gives null IntrinsicValue -> null AOP (L341-346). PredictedFE (L400-443): per-month OLS of FErr on lagSG/lagBM/lagAOP/lagLTG with null_policy='drop' (complete-case estimation), coefficients broadcast to every row in the month; PredictedFE = b_cons + sum(b*rankVAR) using CURRENT ranks — null if any rankVAR null or if the month's regression failed. winsor2(FErr, trim, [1,99], by=time_avail_m) L371 nulls tail values using pandas linear-interpolation quantiles over non-null FErr per month. relrank (stata_replication.py L489-556) = rank(method='average', pct=True) within month, NaN in -> NaN out.
scripts.history_gates: row_num = pl.int_range(pl.len()).over(permno) on the June-only sorted panel (L159): row_num==0 (first June observation per permno) forces ceq_ave=ceq (L164-166) — a per-permno row-position rule. Implicit history: SG needs 60 prior SMT rows (position shift(60), L128-130, computed BEFORE the June filter on the raw monthly SMT panel with NO gap fill); l12_ceq needs the immediately preceding June ROW (shift(1) on June-only panel, L158 — previous June only if no June is skipped); FErr/lag ranks need the permno present 12 calendar months later via +12mo self-joins (L356-365, L384-393, time-based not position-based).
scripts.extra_row_filters: June-only: time_avail_m month==6 (L133). Screens (L252-261, hard row drops BEFORE all cross-sectional ops): ceq>0 & ceq non-null & (|ROE|<=1 or ROE null) & (|FROE1|<=1 or FROE1 null) & (k<=1 or k null) & datadate month>=6 & feps1 non-null & feps2 non-null. IBES prep: froe1 = fpi=='1' & statpers month==5 & fpedats non-null & fpedats>statpers+30d, time_avail_m shifted +1mo (L50-59); froe2 = fpi=='2' & statpers May, +1mo (L70-74); LTG = fpi=='0', no month filter, no offset (L83-84).
wide_grid_divergence_risks: SG = sale/sale.shift(60).over(permno) is POSITION-based on the un-gap-filled monthly SMT panel (L127-130); a calendar 60-month wide-grid lag diverges wherever a permno's SMT months have gaps (shift(60) then reaches >60 calendar months back).

l12_ceq = ceq.shift(1) on the June-only panel (L158): 'previous June row', not calendar t-12; if a firm skips a June, legacy averages with a 2+ year old ceq while a calendar lag yields null (and via L167-169 the null branch would use current ceq instead).

Per-permno first-row rule row_num==0 -> ceq_ave=ceq (L159-172) is row-position logic a full-grid engine cannot express without tracking each permno's first surviving June observation in the SCREENED sample.

All cross-sectional ops (winsor2 trim by month L371, relrank L376-381, per-month OLS L400-421) run on the June+screened sample ONLY; evaluating them over a full month x permno grid (or unfiltered monthlyCRSP universe) changes quantile cuts, ranks, and regression coefficients.
FROE3's LTG-null fallback to FROE2 (L229-239) is a conditional fill — an engine that zero-fills LTG or evaluates the formula branch over the full grid manufactures FROE3 where legacy has no row.

Monthly tiling (L449-462) copies each June value into the next 11 months even past a stock's delisting; legacy CSV contains rows OUTSIDE the CRSP listing span — an engine that masks to the listing span drops rows legacy keeps, while an engine grid that ends at the sample edge truncates the last year's tiling.
Universe class (c): base is SignalMasterTable (shrcd 10/11/12, exchcd 1/2/3); unfiltered monthlyCRSP changes both row support and the cross-sectional estimation samples.

12-month lags for FErr and lagged ranks are time-based self-joins (+12mo offset, L356-365/L384-393) on the screened June set — the lag exists only if the permno passed the screens in BOTH Junes; grid-wide calendar lags of unscreened values diverge.

scripts.universe_source: other (a_aCompustat-driven: annual Compustat keyed by gvkey L40-61; SignalMasterTable left-joined only to fetch exchcd L65-68; final monthly support = per-permno span of annual time_avail_m obs +12mo padding — never intersected with CRSP/SMT monthly rows)
scripts.fill_semantics: Three fills. (1) Annual gap fill: fill_date_gaps_pl(gvkey, fyear_date, '12mo') at L76 inserts null rows for missing fiscal years strictly inside each gvkey's [min,max] fyear span; then fyear fill_null(forward).over(gvkey) L77 (note: forward fill of fyear onto the backbone rows — with 12mo spacing this labels inserted rows with the PRIOR fyear). (2) tempCFO conditional fill (L95-104): oancf if non-null else fopt - d(act) + d(che) + d(lct) - d(dlc) using l1_* calendar-year lags. (3) Monthly expansion: fill_date_gaps_pl(permno, time_avail_m, '1mo', end_padding='12mo') at L215-221 builds each permno's monthly backbone from FIRST annual obs to LAST annual obs +12 months, then AbnormalAccruals fill_null(forward).over(permno) L224-229 — unlimited forward fill within that span (a skipped fiscal year keeps the stale value for the whole gap), hard stop exactly 12 months after the final annual observation. save_predictor drops the leading nulls.
scripts.nan_aggregation: Lags via stata_multi_lag(fill_gaps=False) on the pre-gap-filled annual panel (L80-89, L116-125) = true fiscal-year calendar lags within gvkey span; missing prior year -> null lag -> null ratio. winsor2 trim [0.1,99.9] by fyear (L138) nulls each temp variable INDEPENDENTLY (per-variable trim, not row deletion, despite the comment at L136). OLS per (fyear,sic2) mode='residuals' null_policy='drop' (L151-162): any null among tempAccruals/tempInvTA/tempDelRev/tempPPE -> null residual for that row, row excluded from estimation. _Nobs = count() of NON-NULL tempAccruals per (fyear,sic2) (L166-168) — counts target nulls out but does NOT require regressor completeness.
scripts.history_gates: Group-size gate: filter _Nobs>=6 per (fyear,sic2) at L176 (Xie 2001 minimum). Implicit: every ratio needs the prior fiscal-year row within the gvkey span (l1_at etc.).
scripts.extra_row_filters: NASDAQ exclusion: filter ~((exchcd==3)&(fyear<1982)) at L179-181 — Kleene-logic subtlety: rows with NULL exchcd (no SMT match) and fyear<1982 evaluate to null and are DROPPED by polars filter; null exchcd with fyear>=1982 evaluates true and is kept. Dedup: sort(permno,fyear) then group_by(permno,fyear).first() at L190-193. sic2 = floor(numeric(sic)/100), non-numeric sic -> null sic2 forming its own regression group (L144-147).
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Forward-fill cap: legacy ffill stops exactly 12 months after each permno's LAST annual time_avail_m (end_padding='12mo', L219); an engine that forward-fills over the full grid template extends stale values to the grid end — manufactured values beyond legacy support.

Legacy support can extend BEYOND the CRSP listing span (output is never re-intersected with CRSP/SMT monthly rows) and includes permno-months absent from monthlyCRSP; conversely an engine grid restricted to monthlyCRSP rows drops legacy rows.

Cross-sectional machinery (winsor by fyear L138, OLS per fyear x sic2 L151-162, _Nobs>=6 L176) runs on the annual Compustat sample; any change of sample (full-grid evaluation, different universe) changes trims/residuals/group survival.
Kleene-null exchcd filter at L179-181: engines that treat null exchcd==3 as False would KEEP pre-1982 null-exchcd rows that legacy drops.

Lags are gvkey-level (L76-89); a permno-keyed wide grid mis-lags firms whose permno-gvkey mapping changes or where multiple permnos share a gvkey (dedup at L190-193 happens only AFTER the regressions).

fyear forward-fill on inserted annual-backbone rows (L77) mislabels gap rows with the prior fyear — harmless in legacy (those rows have null data and die at save) but an engine reconstructing fyear from calendar dates will assign different fyears to those cells.

scripts.universe_source: m_aCompustat-driven (no SMT/CRSP merge at all; output support = m_aCompustat permno-months with complete formula inputs)
scripts.fill_semantics: tempTXP = txp.fillna(0) at L73 — zero-fill applied ONLY on existing m_aCompustat rows (no grid), before lagging, so lag_tempTXP at L81 is the zero-filled series shifted 12 rows. No other fills. save_predictor drops null Accruals rows.
scripts.nan_aggregation: All lags are groupby(permno).shift(12) POSITION-based with no gap filling (L77-82). Accruals formula (L90-99): any NaN among act/che/lct/dlc/at/dp or their 12-row lags -> NaN (txp exempted via zero-fill). Denominator (at+lag_at)/2; NaN propagates, 0 denominator -> inf survives save_predictor.
scripts.history_gates: none explicit; implicit requirement of 12 prior m_aCompustat rows per permno (position shift).
scripts.extra_row_filters: drop_duplicates(['permno','time_avail_m'], keep='first') at L65.
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Position shift(12) on un-gap-filled m_aCompustat (L77-82): if a firm's Compustat coverage has a monthly gap (missing fiscal years), legacy lags reach >12 calendar months back; a calendar-lag engine yields NaN there (and vice versa manufactures nothing where legacy computed a value from stale data).

txp zero-fill over the FULL grid (engine) vs only-existing-rows (legacy, L73): manufactures tempTXP=0 and lag_tempTXP=0 in cells outside Compustat coverage; masked in the final value only because act/che/lct/dlc/at lags are simultaneously NaN — an engine whose other wide inputs are forward-filled differently can produce values where legacy has none.

Universe class (c) inverted: legacy includes m_aCompustat permno-months regardless of shrcd/exchcd and regardless of presence in monthlyCRSP; an engine grid built from monthlyCRSP drops Compustat-only rows and its unfiltered universe adds nothing here (no SMT gate in legacy).

scripts.universe_source: SignalMasterTable (right join at L80 keeps ALL SMT rows; Compustat vars NaN where unmatched)
scripts.fill_semantics: No fillna/ffill. AccrualsBM initialized to NaN over all rows (L125), then set to 1 only where tempqBM==5 & tempqAcc==1 (L128), 0 only where tempqBM==1 & tempqAcc==5 (L131), forced back to NaN where ceq<0 (L134; NaN ceq compares False so is unaffected). save_predictor drops NaN -> output rows are exactly the 1s and 0s. Unlike Accruals.py, txp is NOT zero-filled here — missing txp nulls tempacc (L105-113).
scripts.nan_aggregation: Lags: groupby(permno).shift(12) position-based on the SMT-driven merged panel, no gap fill (L96-101). BM = log(ceq/mve_permco) (L92): ceq<=0 -> NaN/-inf. fastxtile (stata_fastxtile.py): replaces +/-inf with NaN (L160), NaN gets NaN quintile; per-month groups with <5 valid obs assign ALL valid rows to bin 1 (L178-181); 2-unique-value groups split into bins 1 and n only (L198-206); otherwise cutpoints = pandas linear-interpolation quantiles at i/n and assignment is STRICTLY-greater-than cutpoint (L209-220). Comparisons against NaN quintiles at L128/L131 are False -> row stays NaN.
scripts.history_gates: none explicit; implicit 12 prior SMT rows per permno for the lag block.
scripts.extra_row_filters: drop_duplicates(['permno','time_avail_m'], keep='first') on m_aCompustat (L66); right join restricts to SMT universe (shrcd 10/11/12, exchcd 1/2/3); ceq<0 -> forced missing (L134).
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Indicator manufacture (class a): the signal is {1,0,NaN}; any engine scheme that defaults the grid to 0 (or evaluates (q==5)&(q==1) with null-as-0 semantics) manufactures 0s on cells where legacy emits nothing — legacy 0 exists ONLY at qBM==1 & qAcc==5 (L131).

Universe class (c): monthly quintile breakpoints are computed within the SMT-merged sample (L117-121); an unfiltered-monthlyCRSP cross-section shifts the cutpoints and thus flips bin membership near boundaries.

fastxtile idiosyncrasies must be replicated exactly: inf->NaN cleaning, <n-valid-obs -> all bin 1, 2-unique-values -> bins {1,n}, strict > cutpoint with pandas linear-interpolation quantiles (stata_fastxtile.py L160-220); a generic qcut/rank-based binning diverges on ties and small months.
Position shift(12) on SMT rows (L96-101) vs calendar lag: diverges where a permno's SMT months are non-contiguous.

scripts.universe_source: SignalMasterTable (right join at L63 keeps all SMT rows)
scripts.fill_semantics: None. AdExp = xad/mve_permco (L71); rows with xad<=0 set to NaN (L74; NaN xad compares False and is already NaN from the division). save_predictor drops NaN rows, so output support = SMT rows with xad>0 and computable ratio.
scripts.nan_aggregation: Elementwise division, NaN propagates. xad>0 & mve_permco==0 -> inf, which is NOT null and survives save_predictor. No lags, no means.
scripts.history_gates: none
scripts.extra_row_filters: xad<=0 -> missing (L74); SMT universe via right join (L63).
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Universe class (c): SMT filter (shrcd 10/11/12, exchcd 1/2/3) vs unfiltered monthlyCRSP.
If the engine's wide xad input is forward-filled beyond m_aCompustat's monthly-expansion window, AdExp values are manufactured outside legacy support (class a).

The xad<=0 mask must use NaN-as-False comparison semantics; treating null xad as passing/failing differently is harmless here only because the division already yields NaN — but an engine that zero-fills xad would turn xad=NaN cells into masked-vs-computed discrepancies.

scripts.universe_source: SignalMasterTable (base panel L70; IBES fpi=='1' left-joined on [tickerIBES, time_avail_m] L77)
scripts.fill_semantics: None. l_meanest = groupby(permno)['meanest'].shift(1) at L91 (position-based, sorted permno/time L85, no gap fill). AnalystRevision = meanest/l_meanest (L94). save_predictor drops NaN rows.
scripts.nan_aggregation: NaN in current or 1-row-lagged meanest -> NaN. l_meanest==0 -> inf survives save_predictor. Note the lag is over permno while the IBES join is by tickerIBES: if two permnos share a tickerIBES both carry the same meanest; the lag itself is per-permno rows.
scripts.history_gates: none explicit; implicit 1 prior SMT row per permno.
scripts.extra_row_filters: IBES restricted to fpi=='1' (L43); SMT universe as base.
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Universe class (c): SMT (shrcd/exchcd filtered) vs unfiltered monthlyCRSP — also, meanest attaches via tickerIBES which only exists on SMT rows; a monthlyCRSP grid lacking the tickerIBES mapping cannot reproduce the join.

shift(1) is position-based over SMT rows (L91): a permno with a gap in SMT months gets its last-available-month estimate as the 'lag' (revision measured across the gap); a calendar 1-month lag yields NaN there.
No fills anywhere: an engine that forward-fills meanest across months manufactures revisions == 1.0 in months where legacy has no IBES row for either numerator or denominator.

scripts.universe_source: m_aCompustat-driven (no SMT/CRSP merge; NO dedup step, unlike Accruals.py)
scripts.fill_semantics: None. l12_at = groupby(permno)['at'].shift(12) at L63 (position-based, no gap fill). AssetGrowth = np.where(l12_at==0, NaN, (at-l12_at)/l12_at) at L66-70 — explicit NaN on zero denominator (comparison NaN==0 is False so NaN lags flow through the formula to NaN naturally). save_predictor drops NaN rows.
scripts.nan_aggregation: NaN at or l12_at -> NaN result; l12_at==0 explicitly mapped to NaN (never inf), which the engine must replicate (a plain division would emit +/-inf and survive the NaN-drop).
scripts.history_gates: none explicit; implicit 12 prior m_aCompustat rows per permno.
scripts.extra_row_filters: none (notably NO drop_duplicates — duplicate permno-months in m_aCompustat, if present, would shift the 12-row lag off-calendar)
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Position shift(12) on un-gap-filled m_aCompustat (L63): coverage gaps make legacy reach >12 calendar months back; calendar-lag engine gives NaN instead.
Universe: legacy support is m_aCompustat permno-months with no shrcd/exchcd screen; an engine grid keyed to monthlyCRSP drops Compustat-only rows and cannot add any (no SMT gate exists to relax).
Zero-denominator must be NaN, not inf (L66-70): an engine that divides then NaN-drops keeps inf rows that legacy suppresses.
Absence of dedup: if m_aCompustat ever carries duplicate permno-months, legacy's lag alignment is row-based and idiosyncratic; a grid engine (one cell per permno-month) cannot reproduce it.

scripts.universe_source: SignalMasterTable (right join at L39 keeps all SMT rows; m_aCompustat supplies datadate/ceqt)
scripts.fill_semantics: me_datadate construction (L51-62): me_datadate = mve_permco.shift(6) over permno (position-based); it is NULLED unless the 6-row-shifted time_avail_m falls in the same calendar month as datadate (Period('M') equality, L55-59); the surviving matches are then groupby(permno).ffill()'d (L62) — UNLIMITED forward fill along the permno's SMT rows, so the last matched market equity persists for years if later datadates never re-match. BM = log(ceqt/me_datadate) (L71); dropna(BM) at L86; manual save with sort_index (L90-93).
scripts.nan_aggregation: log of non-positive ceqt/me ratio -> NaN (negative ceqt dropped, comment L69-70); NaN ceqt, NaN me_datadate, or no prior match -> NaN. ceqt>0 with me_datadate==0 -> log(inf)=inf survives the dropna. The match-guard itself: rows where shifted time != datadate month get NaN before ffill.
scripts.history_gates: none explicit; implicit: a BM value requires at least one past SMT row (>=6 rows back) whose 6-row shift landed exactly on the datadate month.
scripts.extra_row_filters: none beyond the SMT right join (L39) and the NaN drop at L86.
wide_grid_divergence_risks: The shift(6)-equals-datadate-month guard (L51-59) is position-based: when a permno's SMT months have gaps, the 6-ROW shift lands on the wrong calendar month, fails the equality, and legacy silently skips that market-equity update (staler ffill value persists); a calendar-correct 6-month wide-grid lag MATCHES more datadates and produces different (fresher) me_datadate — this is the central divergence of this script.

Unlimited ffill (L62) is confined to the permno's SMT row sequence; ffill over the full grid template extends me_datadate (and hence BM, wherever ceqt is also carried) beyond the last SMT listing month — manufactured values outside the listing span (class a).
Universe class (c): SMT right join (shrcd 10/11/12, exchcd 1/2/3) vs unfiltered monthlyCRSP.
inf preservation: legacy writes log(ceqt/0)=inf rows (dropna at L86 removes only NaN); an engine masking infs diverges on those cells.

scripts.universe_source: other (m_aCompustat INNER-joined to raw monthlyCRSP on permno+time_avail_m, line 64 — no SignalMasterTable, so NO shrcd/exchcd filter; universe = Compustat-coverage months that also have a CRSP row)
scripts.fill_semantics: All fills are within-row fallbacks on the merged (Compustat-and-CRSP) rows only: txditc fillna(0) line 86; tempPS = pstk -> pstkrv -> pstkl (lines 89-91); tempSE = seq -> ceq+tempPS -> at-lt (lines 96-104). tempBE = tempSE + txditc - tempPS (line 107) so NaN tempPS or tempSE still propagates to NaN despite the txditc zero-fill. tempDecME = groupby(permno, calendar-year).transform('min') of December-only tempME=|prc|*shrout (lines 78-82), i.e. the December ME is broadcast to all months of the same permno-year THAT EXIST IN THE MERGED PANEL.
scripts.nan_aggregation: transform('min') skips NaN (no December row in merged panel => tempDecME NaN for whole permno-year). Lag lookups are left-merges on exact dates t-12 / t-17 (lines 113-137): missing calendar month => NaN lag. Division guards: np.where(lagDecME==0, NaN, tempBE/lagDecME) lines 149-159 — NaN==0 is False so NaN lag falls into division and yields NaN. Month selector np.where(month>=6, bm_l12, bm_l17) line 162 evaluates both branches, picks one.
scripts.history_gates: none explicit; effective gate is existence of the merged-panel row at exactly t-12 (months >= 6) or t-17 (months < 6) carrying a non-null tempDecME
scripts.extra_row_filters: drop_duplicates(permno,time_avail_m, keep=first) on Compustat (line 51); inner merge with monthlyCRSP (line 64). No price/exchange/shrcd filters.
wide_grid_divergence_risks: December-ME broadcast domain: legacy broadcasts DecME only over rows surviving the Compustat-inner-join; if a permno's December month lacks a Compustat row, legacy has tempDecME=NaN for the whole year, while an engine computing DecME on the full CRSP grid would find it — manufacturing BMdec values legacy never produces.

Lag lookup domain: l12/l17 tempDecME exist only if the t-12/t-17 month row exists in the merged panel; a full-grid engine that gap-fills or forward-fills DecME across the grid would populate lags legacy leaves NaN.

txditc fillna(0) evaluated over the full grid manufactures txditc=0 outside Compustat coverage; harmless only if the engine also lets NaN tempSE/tempPS propagate to tempBE — any indicator/coalesce reordering breaks this.

Universe: legacy is Compustat-inner-CRSP with NO shrcd/exchcd filter; an engine defaulting to SignalMasterTable filtering (shrcd 10/11/12, exchcd 1/2/3) would drop legacy rows, while unfiltered monthlyCRSP alone would keep rows legacy drops for lack of Compustat.

scripts.universe_source: SignalMasterTable (m_aCompustat inner-joined to SMT on permno+time_avail_m, line 54; SMT supplies mve_permco and the shrcd/exchcd universe)
scripts.fill_semantics: No fills at all. temp = che - dltt - dlc - dc - dvpa + tstkp (lines 61-72): polars null propagation means ANY missing component nulls the row. EBM = (ceq+temp)/(mve_permco+temp) line 75-81; BP = (ceq+tstkp-dvpa)/mve_permco line 84-85; BPEBM = BP - EBM line 89. Dedup is polars group_by(permno,time_avail_m).first() line 48 with default maintain_order=False — which duplicate survives is order-nondeterministic (unlike pandas keep='first' scripts).
scripts.nan_aggregation: Pure null propagation, no lag or mean aggregation. Note polars Float64 division by zero yields +/-inf (not null): mve_permco+temp==0 gives EBM=inf which PASSES save_predictor's is_not_null filter and is written to CSV — there is no division-by-zero guard.
scripts.history_gates: none
scripts.extra_row_filters: dedup one row per permno-month (line 48); inner join with SignalMasterTable (line 54). No other filters.
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Universe class (c): legacy inherits SMT's shrcd 10/11/12 & exchcd 1/2/3 filter via the inner join; an engine on unfiltered monthlyCRSP emits extra permno-months.
Zero-denominator handling: legacy writes +/-inf rows to CSV (polars float division, no guard); an engine that maps division-by-zero to null silently drops rows legacy keeps.

Per-factor: BPEBM requires both BP and EBM non-null (union of all 8 inputs); EBM alone needs {che,dltt,dlc,dc,dvpa,tstkp,ceq,mve_permco}. An engine coalescing any component to 0 on the full grid manufactures values where legacy propagates null.

scripts.universe_source: m_aCompustat-driven (no CRSP or SMT merge anywhere; output universe is every deduped m_aCompustat permno-month with computable book equity)
scripts.fill_semantics: Within-row fallbacks over all m_aCompustat rows: txditc fillna(0) line 72; tempPS = pstk -> pstkrv -> pstkl (lines 76-78); tempSE = seq -> (ceq+tempPS) -> (at-lt) (lines 82-84, note ceq+NaN tempPS = NaN so that branch silently falls through to at-lt). book_equity = tempSE + txditc - tempPS (line 90): NaN tempPS propagates even when tempSE came from seq.
scripts.nan_aggregation: Row-wise NaN propagation only; no lags. Division guard np.where(book_equity==0, NaN, at/book_equity) lines 93-97; NaN==0 is False so NaN book_equity flows through division to NaN.
scripts.history_gates: none
scripts.extra_row_filters: drop_duplicates(permno,time_avail_m, keep=first) line 66 only. No exchange/shrcd/price/SIC filters.

Annual rows are then expanded to 12 monthly rows (time_avail_m .. +11 months, L104-119); per (gvkey, month) keep the row with the LATEST datadate (L122-123); per (permno, month) keep first after sorting non-missing-EquityDuration first, then gvkey, datadate (L128-135). dropna(EquityDuration) L149; manual to_csv.
scripts.nan_aggregation: MD_Part1/PV_Part1 = python sum() of 10 discounted tempCD terms (L88-93): NaN in any term propagates (all terms share tempRoE ancestry, so it is all-or-nothing). Division by tempME = prcc_f*csho (L96-99): missing price or shares -> NaN. temp_g_eq missing is silently converted to 0-growth in projections rather than propagating.
scripts.history_gates: implicit: requires a prior-fyear ceq within the same gvkey (positional shift(1) on the annual panel, L50) — the first annual observation per gvkey never yields a value; a missing fiscal year makes the 'lag' a stale non-adjacent year.
scripts.extra_row_filters: Dedup rules only: per gvkey-month keep max datadate (L122-123); per permno-month keep one row prioritizing non-missing EquityDuration then lowest gvkey/datadate order (L128-135).
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Universe: pure Compustat annual data expanded to months with NO CRSP/shrcd/exchcd screen and NO listing-span bound — the 12-month expansion can emit values after delisting or before CRSP coverage; engine's monthlyCRSP grid differs in both directions (class a/c).
fillna(0) on sales growth manufactures projections for firm-years with missing sale; an engine propagating NaN growth instead drops these rows (class a).
Positional shift(1) over fyear within gvkey: fiscal-year gaps silently use a stale prior year as the lag; a calendar-12-month engine lag diverges on gappy histories (class d).

The two-stage dedup (latest datadate per gvkey-month, then non-missing-first per permno-month) must be replicated exactly for multi-gvkey permnos and overlapping fiscal years; simple 12-month forward-fill of the latest annual value is not equivalent when a newer datadate has NaN EquityDuration but an older one does not.

scripts.fill_semantics: Indicator over every SMT row: exchcd lags 1..12 via POSITIONAL groupby('permno').shift(i) with NO gap filling (L30-31); ExchSwitch = ((exchcd==1 & any lag in {2,3}) | (exchcd==2 & any lag==3)).astype(int) (L38-49). NaN exchcd or NaN lags compare False, so the signal is 0/1 with NO NaN ever — every SMT permno-month gets a row (manual to_csv at L68, no save_predictor NaN-drop, though none would drop).
scripts.nan_aggregation: Comparisons treat NaN as False: isin([2,3]) and ==3 on NaN lags are False; a permno's first 12 months therefore emit 0, not NaN. any(axis=1) over 12 boolean lag columns.
scripts.history_gates: none — no minimum history; rows with fewer than 12 (or zero) available lags still output 0.
scripts.extra_row_filters: none
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Zero-manufacturing (class a, acute): legacy 0s exist exactly on SMT rows; an engine evaluating the indicator over the full month x permno template emits 0s outside listing spans and in shrcd/exchcd-excluded months, inflating the output universe.

Universe/exchcd values: SMT restricts exchcd to 1/2/3; unfiltered monthlyCRSP contains other/negative exchcd codes, changing both the current-exchange condition and the lag membership tests (class c).
Positional shift(i) vs calendar lags: any month gap inside a permno's SMT span makes lag_i reach further back in calendar time than i months; a calendar-lag engine diverges on gappy panels (class d).
Because the signal is dense 0/1 (never NaN), save-side NaN-dropping cannot mask engine over-coverage — every extra grid cell becomes a visible spurious 0.

scripts.fill_semantics: No fillna/gap-filling anywhere. ExclExp = int0a - epspiq (L45); either side NaN -> NaN. Winsorization L48-50: pooled FULL-SAMPLE quantiles q(0.01)/q(0.99) via pandas .quantile (skipna, linear interpolation) computed over ALL permno-months at once (not per month), then np.clip — despite the comment saying 'trim', values are CLIPPED to the cutoffs, not dropped. np.clip(NaN)=NaN so NaNs pass through and are dropped at L54.
scripts.nan_aggregation: Simple subtraction propagates NaN (L45). Pooled quantile at L48-49 skips NaN (pandas default). No rolling/mean-over-lags ops.
scripts.history_gates: none
scripts.extra_row_filters: dropna(subset=['gvkey']) on SignalMasterTable (L26); INNER merge with m_QCompustat on [gvkey,time_avail_m] (L30-34) so universe = SMT rows with non-null gvkey that exist in m_QCompustat; IBES int0a attached via LEFT merge on [tickerIBES,time_avail_m] (L38-42). wide_grid_divergence_risks: Pooled 1%/99% winsorization cutoffs (L48-49) are computed over the legacy universe (SMT ∩ non-null gvkey ∩ m_QCompustat inner join). An engine computing the same quantiles over a full monthlyCRSP grid (extra permnos, extra months, manufactured rows) shifts the cutoffs and therefore changes the CLIPPED values of every extreme observation, not just row membership.
Universe class (c): unfiltered monthlyCRSP grid lacks the shrcd/exchcd SMT filter AND the inner-join-to-m_QCompustat restriction; rows with IBES/Compustat data but outside SMT would be manufactured.
Clipping (winsorize) vs the comment's claim of trimming: engine must clip to cutoffs, not drop rows outside them.

scripts.fill_semantics: No fills of any kind. FEPS = meanest verbatim (L89) after LEFT merge of SMT with IBES_EPS_Unadj filtered to fpi=='1' (L43, L77). save_predictor drops null FEPS.
scripts.nan_aggregation: not applicable — pure passthrough of meanest; null where SMT row has no matching (tickerIBES, time_avail_m) in fpi=='1' IBES rows.
scripts.history_gates: none
scripts.extra_row_filters: IBES side restricted to fpi=='1' (L43); universe restricted to SMT rows (left join preserves all SMT rows, non-matches become null and are dropped on save).
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Universe class (c) only: an unfiltered monthlyCRSP grid would emit FEPS for permno-months outside SignalMasterTable (wrong shrcd/exchcd, or months where the permno is not in SMT) wherever a tickerIBES match exists. Within SMT, semantics are trivially replicable — no fills, lags, or aggregations.

scripts.fill_semantics: No fills. FirmAge = groupby(permno).cumcount()+1 (L31) — a per-permno ROW counter over SMT rows, not a calendar-month offset from first observation. If SMT has intra-span month gaps for a permno, cumcount is smaller than months-elapsed.
scripts.nan_aggregation: not applicable — no arithmetic over multiple columns; only the exclusion rule at L40 sets FirmAge=NaN.
scripts.history_gates: none (cumcount is the signal itself, not a gate)
scripts.extra_row_filters: Original-CRSP-firm exclusion (L34-40): tempcrsptime = round((time_avail_m - 1926-07-01).days / 30.44)+1 cast to int; rows where tempcrsptime == FirmAge get FirmAge=NaN, i.e. firms whose row-count age exactly equals months-since-CRSP-inception are excluded. No exchcd/price filters despite exchcd being loaded (L23, unused).
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Class (d): FirmAge is per-permno row position within SMT. An engine counting months since first grid appearance (or cumcount over an unfiltered monthlyCRSP grid, or over a gap-filled template) diverges whenever a permno has missing SMT months mid-span — engine age would run ahead of legacy age.

The L40 exclusion is an EXACT integer equality between the row counter and a days/30.44-rounded calendar counter; any drift in either counter (grid-based age, different rounding of 30.44 division) flips which rows are nulled — this must use round-half-even pandas .round() then int cast, anchored at 1926-07-01.
Class (c): universe = SMT; unfiltered monthlyCRSP adds permnos/months, which both adds rows and changes each added permno's cumcount stream.

scripts.fill_semantics: Two-layer, ORDER-CRITICAL: (1) ret.fillna(0) at L34 applies ONLY to rows physically present in SMT, BEFORE any filtering or gap-filling. (2) stata_multi_lag at L48 (default fill_gaps=True) runs fill_date_gaps on the ALREADY-FILTERED panel (post price/age filter at L43-44), so months removed by the price/history filter or absent from SMT are re-inserted WITH ret=NULL (they never see the fillna(0)). Consequently l1..l5_ret are null whenever the lag lands on such a re-inserted month, and the momentum product (L51-57) is NaN. Zeros exist only where an original SMT row had missing ret AND survived the L44 filter. Gap span = [first,last] of the filtered rows per permno.
scripts.nan_aggregation: Momentum is an explicit product (1+l1)(1+l2)(1+l3)(1+l4)(1+l5)-1 (L51-57): ANY null lag propagates NaN — no skipping, no zero-substitute. Monthly age quintile via pd.qcut(q=5, labels=False, duplicates='drop')+1 per time_avail_m (L60-62): NaN age (gap-filled rows) -> NaN quintile; rows with quintile>1 OR NaN quintile get FirmAgeMom=NaN (L65).
scripts.history_gates: age = groupby(permno).cumcount()+1 computed on FULL SMT rows before filtering (L37-38); rows kept only if age>=12 (L44) — a per-permno ROW-POSITION gate (12th SMT row, not 12 calendar months). The 5 lags additionally require the lag months to exist as real filtered rows (see fill semantics).
scripts.extra_row_filters: Price filter at L43-44: keep if |prc|>=5 OR prc is NaN (missing price PASSES), combined with age>=12. Quintile restriction L65: only youngest-quintile (quintile==1) rows keep a value.
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Class (b)/(a) combined: an engine that zero-fills ret over the full grid then compounds 5 lags manufactures momentum (i) outside the listing span, (ii) across months the $5-price/age filter removed, and (iii) across SMT gaps — legacy yields NaN in all three cases because fill_date_gaps re-inserts them with NULL ret after the fillna(0). The fillna(0)-BEFORE-filter-BEFORE-gap-fill ordering is the load-bearing detail.
Class (d): age is cumcount over SMT rows (pre-filter), so both the >=12 gate and the quintile ranks diverge if the engine counts grid months or counts post-filter rows.

Monthly qcut quintile breakpoints are computed over the filtered universe (price>=5-or-missing, age>=12, SMT); a full-grid or unfiltered-CRSP cross-section shifts the quintile-1 boundary and changes which stocks keep values.
Class (c): SMT universe; engine must also replicate 'missing price passes the $5 filter'.

scripts.fill_semantics: No fills. ForecastDispersion = stdev / abs(meanest) (L91) after LEFT merge of SMT with IBES filtered to fpi=='1' (L44) AND fpedats non-null (L47). CAUTION: numpy division — meanest==0 with stdev>0 yields +inf, which save_predictor does NOT drop (inf is not null in polars), so inf rows reach the CSV; stdev=0/meanest=0 yields NaN and is dropped.
scripts.nan_aggregation: Elementwise division propagates NaN from either stdev or meanest; no multi-column or rolling aggregation.
scripts.history_gates: none
scripts.extra_row_filters: IBES rows must have fpi=='1' (L44) and non-null fpedats (L47); universe = SMT rows (left join, null on no match, dropped on save).
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Class (c): unfiltered monthlyCRSP grid emits values outside SMT wherever tickerIBES matches exist.
inf handling: legacy retains +inf when meanest==0 and stdev>0 — an engine that maps division-by-zero to null (or drops non-finite) silently deletes those rows; one that keeps them matches.
The fpedats non-null pre-filter (L47) changes which IBES rows merge — omitting it manufactures values from stale/invalid forecast records.

scripts.fill_semantics: xad.fillna(0) at L89 — applied AFTER the inner merge of SMT with m_aCompustat (L70), so zeros exist only on rows present in both tables (never on a full grid). All ratio variables (L99-116) use np.where guards: denominator (at or sale) ==0 OR NaN -> NaN. YtempBM=log(mve_permco) and tempBook=log(ceq) map ±inf to NaN (L92-96); log of negatives is NaN.
scripts.nan_aggregation: Per month t, training set = pooled cross-section with time_avail in (t-60, t] (strict lower bound, inclusive of t; L153-161) after dropping rows with ANY of YtempBM + 7 regressors missing (listwise, L163); skipped entirely if <3 training rows (L165). Prediction rows = month-t rows with all 7 regressors non-null (L171) — YtempBM NOT required for prediction, but Frontier = -(YtempBM - fit) (L253-254) is NaN when YtempBM is NaN anyway. FF48 dummies via pd.get_dummies on training set; prediction dummies reindexed to training columns with fill_value=0 (L186-194) — industries unseen in training contribute 0. sklearn LinearRegression WITH intercept plus full dummy set is rank-deficient; sklearn resolves via lstsq minimum-norm — fitted values are well-defined but coefficient identification differs from a drop-one-dummy solver; a replication must reproduce the fitted values, and for prediction rows whose industry was absent from training the all-zero dummy row is NOT in the training span, so the min-norm solution's specific coefficients matter.
scripts.history_gates: none per-permno; the only temporal requirement is the pooled 60-month trailing window with >=3 complete training rows (L159-165).
scripts.extra_row_filters: INNER merge SMT x m_aCompustat (L70); rows with unmappable FF48 dropped (sicff -> NaN, L120-121); final filter ceq non-null AND ceq>0 (L258); NaN Frontier dropped (L264). Optional --max-year test filter (L73-80, off by default).
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Cross-sectional contamination: the 60-month pooled regression coefficients depend on EXACTLY which rows are in the training set. Any universe change (unfiltered monthlyCRSP, gap-filled grid rows, missing the FF48-dropna or the inner-join restriction) perturbs the fit and therefore changes Frontier for EVERY stock in that month, not just the added/removed rows.
xad zero-fill domain (L89) is the SMT∩Compustat inner-join rows; a full-grid fillna(0) would create tempAdv=0 rows wherever sale is (spuriously) available and alter the regression sample.

Rank-deficient design (intercept + full FF48 dummies): predictions must replicate sklearn's minimum-norm lstsq behavior; a solver that drops a reference dummy gives identical fits for seen industries but can differ for prediction rows whose industry has no training observations (their dummy row is all zeros).
Window is (t-60, t] inclusive of the current month — an engine using [t-59, t] or excluding t diverges; the >=3-row and non-empty-prediction skips (L165, L173) leave whole months NaN.

Class (c): universe = SMT; also ceq>0 filter is applied AFTER prediction, so ceq<=0 rows still participate in training via tempBook only when ceq>0 (log NaN otherwise) — effectively training already requires ceq>0 through listwise deletion, but the row survives to output only via L258.

scripts.fill_semantics: No fills. GP = (revt - cogs)/at (L43). CAUTION: no zero-denominator guard — at==0 yields ±inf which dropna (L46) does NOT remove; inf can reach the CSV.
scripts.nan_aggregation: Elementwise arithmetic propagates NaN from revt, cogs, or at.
scripts.history_gates: none
scripts.extra_row_filters: SIC exclusion of financials: keep sic<6000 OR sic>=7000 (L40) after pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') (L37) — non-numeric/missing sic becomes NaN and BOTH comparisons are False, so NaN-sic rows are DROPPED (pandas semantics, not Stata missing-as-+inf).
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Universe is m_aCompustat directly — NOT SignalMasterTable: no shrcd/exchcd filter is applied by this script at all. An engine anchored to SMT-filtered CRSP would UNDER-cover relative to legacy wherever m_aCompustat has permno-months outside SMT; one anchored to unfiltered monthlyCRSP must still inner-restrict to Compustat coverage and apply the SIC screen.
NaN-sic rows are dropped (comparison-False semantics, L40); a Stata-style missing-as-+inf engine would KEEP NaN sic (>=7000 true) — opposite membership.
at==0 produces inf that survives to the CSV; an engine nulling division-by-zero drops those rows.
No dedup on (permno, time_avail_m): if m_aCompustat carries duplicates they all reach the output — the wide grid can only hold one value per cell.

scripts.fill_semantics: No fills. log_xad = np.log(xad) (L72): xad=0 -> -inf, xad<0 -> NaN (warnings suppressed). 12-period lag is a POSITIONAL groupby shift(12) on the deduped, sorted m_aCompustat panel (L75) — NOT calendar-based and NOT gap-filled: if a permno has month gaps, the 'lag' reaches back 12 ROWS, i.e. more than 12 calendar months. GrAdExp = log_xad - log_xad_l12 (L76). Sign/inf cases: current xad in [0,0.1) is nulled by the L91 filter, but lagged xad==0 with current xad>=0.1 gives finite-(-inf)=+inf which SURVIVES to the CSV (save_predictor drops only nulls).
scripts.nan_aggregation: Subtraction propagates NaN; (-inf)-(-inf)=NaN. Monthly size decile via pd.qcut(mve_c, q=10, labels=False, duplicates='drop')+1 per time_avail_m (L82-84): NaN mve_c -> NaN decile.
scripts.history_gates: Implicit: needs a 12th-prior ROW within the permno's m_aCompustat history (positional shift(12), L75) — first 12 rows per permno are NaN.
scripts.extra_row_filters: drop_duplicates on (permno,time_avail_m) keep='first' (L45). Null-out filter L91: xad<0.1 OR tempSize==1 -> GrAdExp=NaN. CRITICAL pandas semantics: NaN xad fails xad<0.1 (not filtered — but log already NaN), and NaN tempSize fails tempSize==1, so m_aCompustat rows WITHOUT an SMT match (mve_c null after the left merge at L57) are NOT excluded by the size screen — they keep their value.
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Positional shift(12) vs calendar 12-month lag: any intra-span gap in a permno's m_aCompustat rows makes the engine's calendar lag read a different (or null) base month than legacy's 12-rows-back value.

Universe is m_aCompustat-driven with SMT only left-joined for mve_c: rows outside SMT pass the size filter (NaN decile != 1) and are emitted — an SMT-anchored engine drops them; an unfiltered-CRSP engine keeps them only if it replicates the NaN-passes-filter comparison semantics.
Size-decile breakpoints are monthly qcut over mve_c on the m_aCompustat∩SMT rows (including rows whose GrAdExp is null); a decile computed over the full CRSP cross-section shifts the decile-1 cutoff.
+inf values (lagged xad==0, current xad>=0.1) survive to the CSV; engines nulling non-finite values diverge.
Class (a): a full-grid engine must not manufacture log_xad or lags outside the m_aCompustat row span; legacy lags exist only where 12 physical prior rows exist.

scripts.fill_semantics: No fills anywhere. All 10 lag variables (rect, invt, ppent, aco, intan, ao, ap, lco, lo, at) use POSITIONAL groupby shift(12) on the deduped, sorted panel (L83-86) — no fill_date_gaps, so intra-span month gaps make the lag reach >12 calendar months back. GrLTNOA = current_ltnoa - lagged_ltnoa - wc_adjustment (L94-129) with denominators at, l12_at, and (at+l12_at)/2 — no zero guards: at==0 or l12_at==0 can yield ±inf that save_predictor does not drop.
scripts.nan_aggregation: Strict propagation: ANY of the 11 current-period inputs (incl. dp) or 10 lagged inputs missing makes the corresponding sum, and hence GrLTNOA, NaN. No skipna, no mean-over-lags.
scripts.history_gates: Implicit 12th-prior-ROW requirement per permno from shift(12) (L86); first 12 rows per permno are NaN.
scripts.extra_row_filters: drop_duplicates on (permno,time_avail_m) keep='first' (L72). Nothing else — no SIC, price, or exchange filters.
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Positional shift(12) vs calendar lag: gaps in a permno's m_aCompustat coverage shift the legacy lag base month relative to a calendar-true engine lag (which would instead be null or a different month).

Universe is m_aCompustat only — no SMT/shrcd/exchcd screen: an SMT-anchored grid under-covers; an unfiltered monthlyCRSP grid must still restrict to Compustat-present cells and must not manufacture values on grid rows without Compustat data (class a).
Zero-denominator at/l12_at cases yield ±inf that legacy writes to the CSV; engines mapping to null diverge.
keep='first' dedup: if duplicates exist, which physical row survives determines both the level values and the row that a later observation's shift(12) lands on.

scripts.fill_semantics: No fills of any kind. No fill_date_gaps, no fillna. Lags are raw positional groupby('permno').shift(12/24) on rows sorted by [permno,time_avail_m] (L59, L64-67) after drop_duplicates([permno,time_avail_m], keep='first') (L55). save_predictor drops null rows only.
scripts.nan_aggregation: avg_l12_l24 = 0.5*(l12+l24) propagates NaN — primary requires BOTH lags (L73-74). Division guard: np.where(denom==0, NaN, ratio) (L77-88); NaN denom falls to else-branch which yields NaN arithmetically. GrSaleToGrInv = sale_growth - invt_growth propagates NaN (L91). Fallback (12m-only growths, L97-109) substituted wholesale wherever primary is NaN (L112-114) — never mixed per-term; fallback itself NaN if l12 missing or ==0.
scripts.history_gates: Positional, not calendar: primary needs >=25 prior rows of the permno in m_aCompustat (shift(24)); fallback needs >=13 rows (shift(12)). If m_aCompustat has month gaps for a permno, shift(12) reaches 12 ROWS back, not 12 months.
scripts.extra_row_filters: none (only drop_duplicates keep='first' at L55; no price/exchange/shrcd filter — output is NOT restricted to the SMT universe)
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Lag alignment: legacy shift(12)/shift(24) is positional over observed m_aCompustat rows (L64-67); a calendar-lag engine diverges for any permno with month gaps in m_aCompustat.

Universe: legacy emits rows wherever m_aCompustat has data — including permno-months outside the shrcd 10/11/12 & exchcd 1/2/3 SMT filter; an unfiltered-monthlyCRSP grid engine both adds and drops rows relative to this set.
If the engine forward-fills sale/invt over the full grid, it manufactures growth rates in months where m_aCompustat has no row (legacy: no row, no output).
Fallback substitution is all-or-nothing at the final-value level (L112-114); an engine that fills each growth term independently (e.g. zero-fills a missing invt_growth) diverges.
Duplicate permno-month rows resolved by keep='first' in file order (L55); engine must pick the identical row.

scripts.fill_semantics: Identical pattern to GrSaleToGrInv with xsga in place of invt: no fill_date_gaps, no fillna; positional groupby shift(12)/shift(24) after sort (L57, L61-64) and drop_duplicates keep='first' (L54). save_predictor drops null rows only.
scripts.nan_aggregation: avg lag = 0.5*(l12+l24) propagates NaN, both lags required for primary (L72-73); np.where(denom==0, NaN, ratio) division guards (L76-87); difference propagates NaN (L90); fallback 12m formula substituted wholesale where primary NaN (L115-119).
scripts.history_gates: Positional: >=25 prior m_aCompustat rows per permno for primary (shift(24)), >=13 for fallback (shift(12)); gaps in the permno's row sequence shift the reference month.
scripts.extra_row_filters: none (drop_duplicates only, L54; no SMT/shrcd/exchcd restriction)
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Positional vs calendar lags: shift(12/24) over observed rows (L61-64) diverges from calendar lags on a full grid wherever m_aCompustat has month gaps.
Universe: output spans the m_aCompustat row set, not SMT and not monthlyCRSP; an unfiltered-monthlyCRSP engine changes the row set both ways.
Forward-filling sale/xsga on a full grid manufactures growth values in months with no legacy Compustat row.
All-or-nothing fallback substitution (L115-119): per-term filling by the engine diverges.
Duplicate resolution keep='first' (L54) must match.

scripts.fill_semantics: Universe = SMT via how='right' merge (L36): every SMT row kept, sale NaN where m_aCompustat has no row. asrol (L60-70) calls fill_date_gaps_pl which adds gap-month rows ONLY within each permno's [min,max] observed span (stata_replication.py L256-271); on those gap rows all columns except permno/time_avail_m are null, and the 36-month rolling mean IS assigned to them and they SURVIVE to output (dropna at L96 keeps them; the shrcd>11 mask at L75 and SIC masks at L82-87 evaluate False on NaN, so gap rows escape every exclusion). No fillna of inputs anywhere.
scripts.nan_aggregation: indsale = groupby(sic3D,month) transform('sum') skips NaN sale and yields 0.0 for all-NaN groups (L49); temp=(sale/indsale)^2 is NaN when sale NaN (L53); tempHerf = transform('sum') of temp skips NaN and yields 0.0 when every firm's sale is missing (L56) — so tempHerf is non-null on EVERY universe row, including rows with missing sale (they inherit the industry sum over other firms). Rolling: polars rolling_mean(36, min_samples=12) averages only non-null window entries (nulls = span-gap months) and requires >=12 of them. Exclusion masks: pandas NaN comparisons are False, so NaN shrcd/tempSIC rows are NOT struck (L75, L82-87).
scripts.history_gates: >=12 non-null tempHerf observations (i.e., >=12 original universe rows) within the trailing 36 calendar months of the permno's gap-filled span (asrol min_samples=12, L69). Note the window is calendar-positional over the gap-filled span, effect starts at the permno's first SMT month.
scripts.extra_row_filters: Herf set NaN if shrcd>11 (L75; NaN shrcd passes). Domain of the zero-fill is ONLY rows present in m_aCompustat after dedup (line 29) — i.e. permno-months with a Compustat record — never a full calendar grid. l12_emp comes from a calendar self-merge on time_avail_m - 12mo (lines 35-42), so a firm with no Compustat row exactly 12 months prior gets l12_emp=NaN and therefore hire=0 (first-year firms emit 0, not NaN). Line 51 then sets hire=NaN (dropped) for year<1965, overriding the zeros.
scripts.nan_aggregation: Division (emp-l12)/(0.5*(emp+l12)) at line 45 propagates NaN, but line 48 immediately replaces any NaN caused by a missing operand with 0. Edge case: emp=0 and l12_emp=0 (both non-missing) gives 0/0=NaN which is NOT zero-filled and is dropped at line 54.

wide_grid_divergence_risks: Class (a) severe: engine evaluating 'if emp is null -> hire=0' over the full month x permno template manufactures zeros outside each firm's m_aCompustat span (before first / after last Compustat record) and for permnos with no Compustat coverage at all; legacy zeros exist only on m_aCompustat rows (line 48 domain).

Class (c): legacy universe is m_aCompustat rows, not SignalMasterTable and not monthlyCRSP; an unfiltered monthlyCRSP grid both adds cells (CRSP-only months would wrongly get 0 under naive fillna) and can drop cells (Compustat rows without a CRSP grid entry disappear).

Calendar lag: the self-merge lag (lines 35-42) equals shift(12) only on a gapless calendar grid; if engine's grid is the full template this matches, but the resulting NaN lag must feed the zero-fill (hire=0), not row exclusion.
The year<1965 mask (line 51) must be applied AFTER the zero-fill, otherwise pre-1965 zeros leak into output.

Class (c): inner SMT merge means shrcd 10/11/12 & exchcd 1/2/3 universe; on unfiltered monthlyCRSP the tempN>=5 gate, the mean, and membership all shift.

Ordering trap: tempN>=5 (lines 51-52) is evaluated before dropping at-NaN and ppe-NaN rows (55-56), so the gate counts rows that are later excluded from the mean; replicating the gate on the post-drop sample diverges.

sic2D = str(sicCRSP)[:2] (lines 47-48) is STRING truncation: for SIC codes with <4 digits (e.g. 700 -> '70', 70 -> '70', float-formatted '7.0' -> '7.') this differs from sicCRSP//100; engine must replicate the exact string semantics and the source dtype of sicCRSP.
year/decade (lines 73-74) are dead code — must NOT introduce any decade grouping.

Class (c): universe is SMT (shrcd/exchcd filtered) intersected with quarterly Compustat; unfiltered monthlyCRSP grid adds/removes cells and changes which lags exist.
Inf handling: engine that maps division-by-zero to NaN (and drops) loses rows legacy keeps as inf.

Coverage-split breakpoints: the per-month qcut on numest (lines 58-61) is computed on the fully filtered merged sample (March FY1, Dec FYE, SMT-matched); computing the median split on any other universe shifts bin membership.

Class (c): SMT inner merge imposes shrcd/exchcd universe AND requires a non-null tickerIBES link at the December (t-3) month specifically; prc must be the December SMT prc with abs() applied (line 64) since prc can be negative bid/ask midpoints.

No dedup: multiple IBES tickers mapping to one permno (or duplicate Compustat rows) can produce duplicate (permno,yyyymm) output rows — a wide grid cannot represent duplicates and must decide a tie-break legacy never made.

scripts.fill_semantics: No fills. save_predictor (save_standardized.py line 52) drops null std_turn rows at the end. Quintile nulling at lines 62-67 uses pl.when(tempqsize>=4).then(None): a NULL tempqsize (mve_c NaN -> qcut NaN) makes the when-condition null (falsy), so the row keeps its std_turn — missing size does NOT null the signal.
scripts.nan_aggregation: tempturn = vol/shrout, mve_c = shrout*|prc| (lines 37-44) propagate null. rolling_std(window_size=36, min_samples=24).over(permno) (lines 47-52): window is the trailing 36 ROWS; nulls inside the window are excluded from the std and do not count toward min_samples — result is null unless >=24 non-null tempturn values in the last 36 rows. pd.qcut per month on mve_c (lines 56-58): NaN mve_c -> null quintile (row keeps std_turn per when-semantics above).
scripts.history_gates: per-permno trailing 36-ROW window requiring >=24 valid observations (min_samples=24, lines 47-52). CRITICAL: gaps are never calendar-filled, so this is row-position based — for a permno with listing gaps the 36-row window spans MORE than 36 calendar months.
scripts.extra_row_filters: std_turn set to null (hence dropped by save_predictor) where per-month mve_c size quintile >= 4, quintiles computed by pd.qcut(q=5,duplicates='drop')+1 over the FULL monthlyCRSP cross-section (lines 55-67)
wide_grid_divergence_risks: Class (d) severe: engine on a gap-filled calendar grid turns the 36-row window into a 36-calendar-month window; legacy (no fill_date_gaps) uses the last 36 observed rows, so any permno with intra-listing gaps gets different windows and different std values, and the min_samples=24 gate binds differently.
Class (a)/(b): zero-filling tempturn where vol or shrout is null both distorts the std and spuriously satisfies min_samples=24; nulls must be excluded from the window computation and its count.

Quintile breakpoints must be computed per month over the unfiltered monthlyCRSP cross-section with NaN mve_c excluded from qcut (lines 56-58); if engine fills mve_c nulls with 0 those rows enter quintile 1 and shift everyone's breakpoints.
Null-quintile keep rule: when(null>=4) is falsy so std_turn is retained (lines 62-67); an engine that nulls the signal when size is missing diverges.

scripts.extra_row_filters: dedup via groupby([permno,time_avail_m]).first() (line 31) — NOTE this takes the first NON-NULL value per column across duplicate rows (column-wise coalescing), NOT the first row wholesale; manufacturing firms only: 2000 <= numeric(sic) <= 3999, with non-numeric/NaN sic excluded because comparisons are False (lines 35-38)

Class (c): universe is m_aCompustat rows (no SMT/shrcd/exchcd filter, no monthlyCRSP requirement); an unfiltered monthlyCRSP grid both adds cells lacking Compustat data and can drop Compustat-only cells.
SIC filter semantics: missing/non-coercible sic must be EXCLUDED (comparison-False, lines 35-38), not treated as 0 or passed through.

Dedup semantics: groupby.first() coalesces first non-null per column across duplicate (permno,month) rows — a keep-first-row dedup (like hire.py line 29) can produce different component values when duplicates differ in null patterns.
at==0 rows produce inf that legacy writes out; an engine mapping div-by-zero to null drops rows legacy keeps.
